title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2026 (Japanese Studies Students)
official_source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan
program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme (embassy recommendation)
duration: One year of study at a designated Japanese university through the Japanese Studies Program course listed in the Course Guide of Japanese Studies Program
description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2026 (Japanese Studies Students) funds international undergraduates who major in Japanese language or Japanese culture to study for one year at designated Japanese universities. Applicants must already have studied Japanese studies for at least one year and must remain enrolled at their home institution on return. MEXT states that it "offers scholarships to international students who wish to study for a period of one year at designated Japanese universities as Japanese Studies Students". title: JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students
degree: Undergraduate, Master's, PhD, Junior College, College of Technology, Specialized Training College, University Preparatory Course, Japanese Language Institute
program_type: Privately-financed student honors scholarship (nominated by the host institution)
duration: 12 months (April to the following March) or 6 months (October to the following March)
description: The JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a stipend for privately financed international students in Japan with excellent academic and character records who face financial difficulties. It is not open for direct application: each educational institution nominates candidates to JASSO, and the number of candidates depends on the institution's international enrolment. The stipend is JPY 48,000 per month at graduate and undergraduate level and JPY 30,000 per month at Japanese language institutes, for 12 or 6 months.

title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan - Standard Program (Open Call)
official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
duration: 12 to 24 months, provided in full month units; the Standard open call runs two rounds a year with arrival windows of 1 April to 30 September 2027 (1st round) and 1 September to 30 November 2027 (2nd round)
description: The JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan (Standard Program) let excellent postdoctoral researchers from other countries conduct cooperative research in Japan with a Japanese host researcher. JSPS runs two open-call rounds a year and awarded 120 fellowships in each FY2027 round. The fellowship pays a maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 and overseas travel insurance. Applications are submitted by the host researcher through the JSPS Electronic Application System, not by candidates directly.

title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term Program (PE), Open Call
official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
program_type: Research fellowship - postdoctoral short-term, open call
description: The Short-term Program (PE) of the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan lets young PhD holders and PhD researchers conduct collaborative research in Japan for between 1 and 12 months. It is restricted to candidates from the United States, Canada, EU member states, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway and Russia, who hold a doctoral degree obtained within the previous six years or are currently enrolled in a doctoral course abroad. title: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term (FY2027, 2nd Recruitment)
official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) - applied for by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution
description: The JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan invite mid-career and senior overseas researchers to Japan for lectures, discussions and exchange activities hosted by a Japanese researcher. The short-term option runs 14 to 60 days and covers a round-trip economy air ticket, a maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day, overseas travel insurance and a host-applied research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000. The candidate does not apply directly: a host researcher in Japan submits the application through the head of their institution.

title: Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Scholarship 2027 (Overseas Candidates)
program_type: Foundation scholarship - monthly stipend plus travel subsidy
duration: Depends on the enrolled programme; stipend begins at the designated month of admission
description: The Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Scholarship for Overseas Candidates is for overseas students scheduled to enrol in a Japanese university or graduate school, and requires a JLPT pass at N3 or above and an independent application to a Japanese institution. The application window for 2027 enrolment runs from 13:00 JST on 1 October 2026 to 13:00 JST on 31 October 2026. The stipend is JPY 100,000 per month for undergraduates and JPY 140,000 per month for master's and doctoral students, and successful applicants may receive a travel-expense subsidy of up to JPY 250,000.

title: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
official_source: Study in NL (Nuffic) — financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and Dutch higher education institutions
duration: One-off payment of EUR 5,000, received in the first year of studies. The scholarship is not described as multi-year or recurring.
description: The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national scholarship programme for bachelor and master students from outside the European Economic Area. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. Study in NL states the scholarship amounts to € 5,000 and is paid in the first year of studies, and explicitly notes that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Institutions set their own application deadlines and their own amount tiers, so the value and the deadline both depend on the institution you apply to.
